item.title: Traffic Committee Reestablished; First Meeting Monday, Oct 12th at Noon
item.description:
Publication date estimated from listing: 2026-10-09

First collected: 2026-10-17 14:48 EDT

Attention Residents,

To address various traffic matters in a more channelized manner, Lancaster Township is reestablishing its Traffic Committee to provide a more structured approach to reviewing traffic-related concerns. This committee is advisory to the Board of Supervisors and no action beyond recommendations to the Board. The Committee will consist of three Township representatives, or their designees: the Township Manager, Public Works Superintendent, and Chief of Police.

Residents are welcome to attend Traffic Committee meetings; however, attendance is not necessary to have your concerns heard. Residents who are unable to attend, or who prefer to provide comments in advance, may submit them by email to Public Works Superintendent Devin Groff at dgroff@twp.lancaster.pa.us. All submitted comments will be documented and provided to Committee members for consideration.

The Committee Chair may read submitted comments aloud, in whole or in part, during the meeting.

Meetings will be held quarterly on the second Monday of January, April, July, and October at noon, coinciding with the regularly scheduled Board of Supervisors meeting day. Meetings will take place in the meeting room at 1240 Maple Avenue, with entrance access from Perry Avenue. An opportunity for public comment will be provided at the conclusion of each meeting.

Click here to find the first agenda and know where to find future agendas. Thank you for your attention.

Lancaster Township Communications

item.title: Keep Leaf Piles Off the Street
item.description:
Publication date estimated from listing: 2026-09-16

First collected: 2026-10-17 14:48 EDT

Residents, we are so excited that you're ready for our curbside leaf collection services this year, but they are not scheduled to begin until October 8th! Do not place any leaves in the street. Property owners may be given a notice if this issue persists.

Until October 8th, we operate our biweekly street sweeping program, click here for our Street Operations Calendar . While our sweeper is cleaning the roads, and sometimes that's a few leaves, the sweeper equipment is not designed for leaf picking. The sweeper will go around these piles as they could cause malfunction or equipment breakdowns. Please help us keep the streets as orderly as possible until leaf collection season by using our biweekly yard waste collection using brown bags or bring them by the woody waste facility during operating hours, here is a calendar for Woody Waste .

Keeping the leaves out of the street and disposing of them in yard waste bags or at the woody waste facility will do a few things:
  • Keeps parking lanes more available for vehicles
  • Allows for better street sweeping through the season
  • Prevents leaves washing away and forming stormwater clogs at inlets
The best thing you can do in the tighter neighborhoods with limited areas to store piles off-street, is to bag them in brown bags for yard waste collection or to store until you can make it out to woody waste. It keeps them stored in a way they won't blow around, out of the way, and if you forget to put them out while brown bags get collected until October 8th, you can always take them to Woody Waste and reuse the bag a few times through the season.

Please make sure you are signed up for the Township E-notify system by clicking HERE and that you are familiar with your leaf collection zone by clicking HERE to see the map. We use the alert box to send out leaf collection communications, and now with E-Notify you can get alerted of those changes. We ask residents keep all leaf piles off the street in collection season until 48 hours from communicated service. This practice also helps minimize the above impacts in the thick of the leaf drop. We know this time of year can be a lot to manage; with your help we can manage it well.

If you have any questions, please first direct them to the Communications and Outreach Coordinator, Tony Dastra, by sending an email with your inquiry to pwadmin@twp.lancaster.pa.us . If you click the link, it will prefill the email and subject.

item.title: North Conestoga Drive Closure Notice
item.description:
Publication date estimated from listing: 2026-09-09

First collected: 2026-10-17 14:48 EDT

We are distributing a paper notice to residents along affected roadways. This news item is to serve as a digital copy that residents can share as needed.

Attention Resident,

During the recent flooding in early September, the highwater caused significant erosion along the Conestoga River. A section of the riverbank has separated and failed, extending to the edge of the roadway. Although the pavement has not visibly failed, the erosion may have affected the ground supporting the roadway. At this time, we do not know how far the damage extends beneath the pavement or how stable the roadway is.

For the safety of the public, the affected section of North Conestoga Drive will be closed to through traffic until further notice.

We understand that residents and businesses in the area still need access. The barricades closing the affected section will be positioned to allow local access where possible. Please be aware that traffic will only be able to travel in one direction through the accessible portion of the roadway, and you may need to adjust your normal travel routes. We appreciate your patience and cooperation as we address this sudden and unfortunate situation. Our priority is to protect the safety of residents, businesses, and motorists while we determine the best course of action.

A map showing the upcoming signage and detour route is attached. Please use caution, follow all posted signs, and allow additional time for travel.

If you have questions regarding the closure, please contact the Public Works Superintendent, Devin Groff, at dgroff@twp.lancaster.pa.us.

Thank you for your patience and understanding,

Lancaster Township Communications

Estimado residente,

Durante las recientes inundaciones de principios de septiembre, el nivel elevado del agua provocó una erosión significativa a lo largo del río Conestoga. Un tramo de la ribera ha cedido y se ha desprendido, extendiéndose hasta el borde de la calzada. Aunque el pavimento no presenta daños visibles, la erosión podría haber afectado el terreno que sirve de base a la carretera. Por el momento, desconocemos el alcance de los daños bajo el pavimento o el grado de estabilidad de la vía.

Por seguridad pública, el tramo afectado de North Conestoga Drive permanecerá cerrado al tráfico de paso hasta nuevo aviso.

Entendemos que los residentes y negocios de la zona necesitan seguir teniendo acceso. Las barreras que cierran el tramo afectado se colocarán de manera que permitan el acceso local siempre que sea posible. Tenga en cuenta que la circulación por la parte accesible de la vía será de sentido único, por lo que es posible que deba modificar sus rutas habituales. Agradecemos su paciencia y colaboración mientras gestionamos esta situación imprevista y desafortunada. Nuestra prioridad es proteger la seguridad de los residentes, los negocios y los conductores mientras determinamos la mejor forma de proceder.

Se adjunta un mapa con la señalización prevista y la ruta de desvío. Le rogamos que extreme las precauciones, respete todas las señales y prevea tiempo adicional para sus desplazamientos.

Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre el cierre, puede ponerse en contacto con el Superintendente de Obras Públicas, Devin Groff, en la dirección dgroff@twp.lancaster.pa.us.

Gracias por su paciencia y comprensión.

Comunicaciones del Municipio de Lancaster

item.title: Bridge Inspection Will Restrict Traffic on EB Route 462 (East King Street) over Conestoga River in Lancaster County
item.description:
Publication date estimated from listing: 2026-09-08

First collected: 2026-10-17 14:48 EDT

Expect a right lane restriction on September 9 from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM.

 Harrisburg, PA – The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) announced today that a bridge inspection will be performed next week on the Route 462 (East King Street) bridge over the Conestoga River at the Lancaster-East Lampeter Township Line in Lancaster County.

Weather permitting, a crew will inspect the bridge on Wednesday, September 9, from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM. There will be a right lane and shoulder restriction on eastbound Route 462 during working hours.

Inspectors plan to view the bridge using a snooper crane from the road.

Travelers are reminded to be alert for this operation, to obey work zone signs, and to use caution when driving through work zones for their safety, as well as for the safety of the inspection crew.

Travelers can check conditions on major roads by visiting www.511PA.com. 511PA, which is free and available 24 hours a day, provides traffic delay warnings, weather forecasts, traffic speed information and access to more than 1,200 traffic cameras. 511PA is also available through a smartphone application for iPhone and Android devices, by calling 5-1-1, or by following regional X alerts. 

Find PennDOT’s planned and active construction projects at www.pa.gov/DOTprojects. Subscribe to PennDOT news and find transportation results in Adams, Cumberland, Dauphin, Franklin, Lancaster, Lebanon, Perry and York counties at www.pa.gov/DOTdistrict8.

item.title: Road Crew Position Opening
item.description:
Publication date estimated from listing: 2026-09-02

First collected: 2026-10-17 14:48 EDT

Lancaster Township Public Works is currently accepting applications for a dependable, motivated, and team-oriented individual to join our Public Works Department as a Road Crew Member.

This full-time position offers the opportunity to work in a hands-on, outdoor environment serving the local community. Ideal candidates will take pride in their work, demonstrate a strong work ethic, and be willing to learn.

Primary Responsibilities Include (but are not limited to):

  • Roadway maintenance and construction
  • Park, property, and building upkeep
  • Vehicle and equipment maintenance (diesel, gas, hydraulic, and small engines)
  • Winter operations, including plowing, salting, and brining
  • Participation in a rotating on-call schedule and all winter weather events

Qualifications:

  • Valid driver's license with the ability to obtain a Class A CDL within one year of employment, training may be provided
  • Must pass pre-employment background check and drug and alcohol testing; random drug and alcohol testing required through employment
  • Prior experience in related fields is preferred but not required

What We Offer:

  • Competitive pay (commensurate with experience)
  • Excellent benefits and pension program
  • Four 10-hour workdays (Monday–Thursday)
  • Paid holidays
  • Vacation, personal, and sick time 

How to Apply:

Applications are available online here:  Application for Employment 

Please mail or hand them in to the Township Office at:
1240 Maple Avenue, Lancaster, PA 17603
OR
Completed applications and resumes may be emailed to Dgroff@twp.lancaster.pa.us.

Questions?

(223)221-7523
Devin Groff, Public Works Superintendent
Lancaster Township
1240 Maple Avenue
Lancaster, PA 17603

item.title: Back to School Reminder
item.description:
Publication date estimated from listing: 2026-08-25

First collected: 2026-10-17 14:48 EDT

It's that time of year, it's back to school! 

With school back in session it is important that travelers remember a few things:

  • Give yourselves extra time in the morning and afternoon to travel. School starting up may cause some delays in your commute, especially as we shake off the summer rust for pick-ups and drop-offs.
  • Obey all school zone signage, school bus stop signs, and other safety measures. We want to make sure all students get in and out of the building safely.
  • As Fall comes, remember that the angle of the sunlight shifts and this could impact your visibility for aspects of your commute. Make sure you operate your vehicle safely no matter the conditions.
Thank you for traveling safely through Lancaster Township, and we hope that all students have a great school year!

item.title: Burrowes Elementary School Zone
item.description:
Publication date estimated from listing: 2026-07-22

First collected: 2026-10-17 14:48 EDT

A message from Burrowes Elementary School, we are also thankful for their work and this partnership to improve safety with the completion of their new building:

"We are excited to share an important safety improvement happening around our school! In partnership with Lancaster Township, PA - Lancaster County, new school zone and traffic safety signs will soon be installed in the streets surrounding our school.

The new signage will include school zone designations with speed limit restrictions to keep folks safe at Burrowes, other School District of Lancaster students, and our entire community.

As the signs are installed, we ask all families and visitors to:

Observe posted speed limits, especially in school zones
Use designated crosswalks when walking with students
Allow extra time during arrival and dismissal as everyone adjusts to the changes

These improvements are part of an ongoing effort to create a safer environment for everyone traveling to and from Burrowes each day.

We appreciate your partnership in helping us keep our students safe.

We also appreciate the advocacy from families in making our community safer.

Together, we can make every trip to and from school a safe one. "

item.title: (UPDATED 7/21) Projected Line Painting Projects
item.description:
Publication date estimated from listing: 2026-07-21

Attention Residents and travelers,

There are several line painting projects that will occur in the Township during the month of July and into August, the dates for these projects are subject to change due to weather conditions, but we have tentative dates and would like to provide a sense of when the work will occur.

  • Unsignalized intersection crosswalks and stop bars will be painted by the Lancaster Township Public Works crew starting July 13th on the East Side and this work will continue into August. 
  • Signalized intersections are scheduled for contracted painting overnight on July 12th to July 14th July 26th to July 29th.
  • Contracted long line painting is scheduled to begin July 27th to July 29th August 3rd to August 5th
Again, these dates could shift due to weather. Thank you for your understanding and patience as we refresh the road markings.

Lancaster Township Communications
